subject: DI04005021

body.en:
Definition / principle

Liquid–liquid extraction separates a dissolved solute by distributing it between the original liquid and another liquid solvent that creates two separable phases. Extract is the solvent-rich product; raffinate is the feed-carrier-rich product.

Detailed theory and conditions

The operation is useful when volatility differences are poor, heat-sensitive materials discourage distillation or a solvent provides useful selectivity. Applications include recovery of organic acids from aqueous streams, purification of selected chemical products and hydrometallurgical extraction using suitable extractants. The solvent normally requires downstream recovery; extraction alone does not necessarily give a pure solute. A light phase is not automatically the extract: which product is extract depends on solvent identity, while top/bottom location depends on density.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Original liquid તથા બીજો solvent બે separable phases બનાવે અને solute તેમના વચ્ચે distribute થાય તે liquid–liquid extraction છે. Solvent-rich product extract અને feed-carrier-rich product raffinate છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Volatility difference ઓછો હોય, heat-sensitive material હોય અથવા solvent useful selectivity આપે ત્યારે extraction ઉપયોગી છે. Aqueous streams માંથી organic acids recovery, chemical purification તથા suitable extractants વડે hydrometallurgical extraction examples છે. Downstream solvent recovery સામાન્ય રીતે જોઈએ; extraction માત્રથી pure solute મળતો નથી. Light phase હંમેશાં extract નથી. Extract solvent identity પરથી અને top/bottom density પરથી નક્કી થાય છે.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Liquid equilibrium specifies compositions of two coexisting liquid phases at given temperature and pressure. A tie line joins the conjugate equilibrium phase compositions.

Detailed theory and conditions

A distribution coefficient compares solute concentration in extract with that in raffinate on a declared basis. It can vary with composition, temperature and association; it is not universally constant. Selectivity compares separation of solute C from feed carrier A between phases. A solvent with high capacity may also dissolve much carrier and give poor selectivity. There must actually be two phases; one homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture cannot by itself define an interphase distribution coefficient. Water/organic systems need explicitly identified aqueous and organic phases.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Given T, P પર બે coexisting liquid phases ની compositions liquid equilibrium દર્શાવે છે. Conjugate equilibrium compositions જોડતી line tie line છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Declared basis પર extract તથા raffinate માં solute concentrations નો ratio distribution coefficient છે. Composition, T તથા association થી તે બદલાઈ શકે છે; universal constant નથી. Selectivity phases વચ્ચે solute C ને carrier A સામે અલગ કરવાની ક્ષમતા દર્શાવે છે. High-capacity solvent carrier પણ ઘણો dissolve કરે તો selectivity નબળી હોઈ શકે છે. બે phases હોવી જરૂરી છે. એક homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture થી interphase coefficient નક્કી ન થાય. Aqueous તથા organic phases સ્પષ્ટ ઓળખો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

title.en: Equilateral triangular coordinates and lever rule
title.gu: Equilateral Triangular Coordinates તથા Lever Rule

h.en: Equilateral triangular coordinates and lever rule
h.gu: Equilateral Triangular Coordinates તથા Lever Rule

body.en:
Definition / principle

An equilateral ternary composition diagram represents mixtures of three components whose fractions add to one. A vertex represents a pure component and the opposite side represents zero fraction of that component.

Detailed theory and conditions

Read a component fraction along lines parallel to the side opposite its vertex. Always identify component names, temperature and mass or mole basis; do not mix the bases. A binary mixture lies on an edge and a ternary mixture lies inside. A mixing point M for streams F and S lies on their straight joining line, closer to the larger stream. The splitting of M into conjugate E and R lies along a measured tie line, not along an arbitrary line to a vertex. Lever-rule product ratios use opposite segment lengths. Mixing line and equilibrium tie line are different geometric objects.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

ત્રણ components ના fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોય તેવી compositions equilateral ternary diagram દર્શાવે છે. Vertex pure component તથા opposite side તે component નો zero fraction છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Vertex ની opposite side ને parallel lines વડે fraction વાંચો. Component names, T તથા mass/mole basis લખો; બંને bases mix ન કરો. Binary mixture edge પર અને ternary mixture અંદર આવે છે. F તથા S નું mixing point M straight joining line પર તથા larger stream ની નજીક આવે છે. M ના E, R products measured tie line પર હોય છે; vertex તરફ arbitrary line નહીં. Lever rule માં opposite segment lengths નો ratio લેવાય છે. Mixing line તથા equilibrium tie line જુદાં છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

title.en: Three liquids:one partially soluble pair and T/P effects
title.gu: Three Liquids:One Partially Soluble Pair તથા T/P અસર

h.en: Three liquids:one partially soluble pair and T/P effects
h.gu: Three Liquids:One Partially Soluble Pair તથા T/P અસર

body.en:
Definition / principle

A Type-I ternary system has one binary pair with limited mutual solubility, while the third component is mutually miscible with the other two over the stated range.

Detailed theory and conditions

The partially miscible pair creates a miscibility gap whose ternary boundary is the binodal curve. Compositions within the two-phase region split along tie lines; the two branches approach one another at a plait point where the phase distinction disappears. Tie lines are generally not horizontal and their slopes must come from data. For many upper-critical-solution-temperature systems, heating shrinks the miscibility gap, but lower-critical and more complex behavior also exist; do not claim that temperature always increases mutual solubility. Ordinary pressure has a smaller effect on nearly incompressible liquid equilibrium, unless high pressure, gas solubility or special phase behavior is involved. The diagram here is schematic, not measured acetic-acid/benzene/water data.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Stated range માં એક binary pair limited mutual solubility ધરાવે અને third component બંને સાથે miscible હોય તે Type-I ternary system છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Partially miscible pair થી miscibility gap બને છે; તેની ternary boundary binodal curve છે. Two-phase region નું mixture tie line અનુસાર split થાય છે. Plait point પાસે બંને phases નો difference અદૃશ્ય થાય છે. Tie lines હંમેશાં horizontal નથી; actual data જોઈએ. ઘણા upper-critical systems માં heating થી gap ઘટે છે, પરંતુ lower-critical/complex behavior પણ હોય છે. Temperature થી miscibility હંમેશાં વધે એવું ન કહો. Nearly incompressible liquids પર ordinary pressure ની અસર સામાન્ય રીતે ઓછી છે; high pressure/gas solubility/special behavior exceptions છે. આ schematic છે, measured acid/benzene/water data નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

A Type-II ternary system has two binary pairs with limited mutual solubility at the specified conditions.

Detailed theory and conditions

Miscibility gaps therefore appear on two binary edges rather than only one. The two-phase region and its conjugate branches must be obtained from equilibrium data; they need not resemble the simple Type-I cap or share its plait-point construction. Tie lines still join coexisting phases and all phase compositions must sum to one. The number of partially miscible binary pairs does not by itself imply three liquid phases. The supplied diagram is a topology sketch identifying the two affected edges, not a source of quantitative stage compositions.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified conditions પર બે binary pairs limited mutual solubility ધરાવે તે Type-II ternary system છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

બે binary edges પર miscibility gaps મળે છે. Two-phase region તથા conjugate branches actual equilibrium data પરથી નક્કી કરો; તે Type-I cap/plait construction જેવી હોવી જરૂરી નથી. Tie lines coexisting phases જોડે છે અને phase fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોવો જોઈએ. બે partially miscible binary pairs એટલે ત્રણ liquid phases નહીં. Sketch બે affected edges ઓળખાવે છે; quantitative stage compositions માટે data નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

An extraction solvent must create a favorable solute distribution and sufficiently separable liquid phases while remaining recoverable and safe.

Detailed theory and conditions

Evaluate selectivity, capacity, mutual solubility with feed carrier, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, chemical stability and ease of regeneration. Adequate density difference helps settling; very stable emulsions or low interfacial tension may hinder disengagement. Low viscosity aids transfer and pumping, but solvent loss/product contamination may still dominate economics. Include toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost and compatibility. A high distribution coefficient alone is insufficient if the solvent is difficult to separate or recover.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Favorable solute distribution તથા separable phases સાથે recoverable અને safe હોય તે extraction solvent પસંદ કરવો.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Selectivity, capacity, feed carrier સાથે mutual solubility, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, stability તથા regeneration જુઓ. Density difference settling ને મદદ કરે છે. Stable emulsion/low interfacial tension disengagement મુશ્કેલ કરી શકે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping સુધારે છે પણ solvent loss/contamination ખર્ચાળ હોઈ શકે છે. Toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost તથા compatibility ગણો. High distribution coefficient માત્ર પૂરતો નથી.

title.en: Derivation:single-stage extraction balance and lever rule
title.gu: Derivation:Single-stage Extraction Balance તથા Lever Rule

h.en: Derivation:single-stage extraction balance and lever rule
h.gu: Derivation:Single-stage Extraction Balance તથા Lever Rule

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady equilibrium stage or completed batch; no reaction/evaporation; F, S, E, R are masses or mass rates on the same basis. zF, zS, zM and wE, wR are solute mass fractions. Equilibrium endpoints must be known independently.

  1. Total balance and mixed composition.

  2. Component balance after phase separation.

  3. Eliminate raffinate flow.

  4. Solve the two product flows.

  5. Rearrange to the lever rule along the E–R tie line.

  6. Also close carrier and solvent balances. A solute-only result is not enough if the assumed ternary endpoints are inconsistent.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: total balance → solute balance → eliminate R → solve E, R; mention measured tie-line endpoints. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady equilibrium stage અથવા completed batch, no reaction/evaporation. F, S, E, R same-basis masses/mass rates છે. zF, zS, zM તથા wE, wR solute mass fractions છે. Equilibrium endpoints અલગથી જાણીતા હોવા જોઈએ.

  1. Total balance તથા mixed composition.

  2. Phase separation પછી component balance.

  3. Raffinate flow eliminate કરો.

  4. બંને product flows શોધો.

  5. E–R tie line માટે lever rule મેળવો.

  6. Carrier તથા solvent balances પણ close કરો. Inconsistent ternary endpoints માટે solute-only result પૂરતો નથી.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

First use general stage balances. For the closed-form result assume insoluble carrier flow L remains constant, pure fresh solvent Sj at each stage, negligible mutual solubility and linear equilibrium Yj=mXj on solute-free mass ratios. X=solute/carrier, Y=solute/solvent.

  1. General total and solute balances at stage j.

  2. Write the component balance without assuming constant total raffinate.

  3. Under the stated carrier model, pure solvent has zero entering solute.

  4. Insert the equilibrium ratio and solve.

  5. Successive fresh-solvent contacts multiply the residual factors.

  6. For equal solvent portions and constant m, recovery follows from the residual solute.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: one-stage carrier balance → equilibrium substitution → recurrence → two-stage application. Do not use the simplified formula for mutually soluble ternary phases. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

પહેલાં general stage balances લો. Closed form માટે constant insoluble carrier L, pure fresh solvent Sj, negligible mutual solubility તથા solute-free mass ratios પર Yj=mXj લો. X=solute/carrier, Y=solute/solvent છે.

  1. Stage j ના general total તથા solute balances.

  2. Total raffinate constant માન્યા વગર component balance.

  3. Stated carrier model માં pure solvent નું entering solute zero છે.

  4. Equilibrium ratio મૂકી solve કરો.

  5. Successive fresh-solvent contacts ના residual factors multiply કરો.

  6. Equal solvent portions તથા constant m માટે residual પરથી recovery મેળવો.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

body.en:
Definition

A mechanically mixed vessel that disperses one liquid phase in another to create extraction contact; phase separation completes the stage.

Principle

Agitation increases interfacial area and renews the liquid films so solute moves toward its equilibrium distribution.

Construction

A vessel contains an impeller on a driven shaft, baffles, feed/solvent connections and an outlet for the contacted mixture. A compatible shaft seal and suitable containment limit solvent escape. For batch use the vessel can also allow settling after agitation stops; for continuous use a separate gravity settler normally receives the dispersion. The mixer outlet is therefore a two-phase mixture, not automatically two separated product streams.

Working

Feed and solvent contact under controlled mixing. One phase forms droplets in the other and solute crosses the enlarged interface. Contact continues for the required residence time, but vigorous mixing does not guarantee equilibrium. The dispersion is then settled and the conjugate phases withdrawn separately. Batch operation alternates mixing and settling; continuous mixer–settler operation separates those functions into adjacent units. Excessive shear can produce difficult emulsions and increase carryover.

Applications

Stagewise liquid extraction and a mixer section in mixer–settler cascades.

Limitations and precautions

Power, sealing, emulsification and residence time matter. The hazardous-solvent SOP and rated containment govern actual use.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

એક liquid phase ને બીજામાં disperse કરીને extraction contact આપતું mechanically mixed vessel છે. Phase separation થી stage પૂર્ણ થાય છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Agitation interfacial area વધારી liquid films renew કરે છે; solute equilibrium distribution તરફ જાય છે.

રચના (Construction)

Vessel માં driven shaft/impeller, baffles, feed/solvent connections તથા contacted-mixture outlet હોય છે. Compatible seal/containment solvent escape limit કરે છે. Batch માં agitation બંધ કર્યા પછી settling એ જ vessel માં થઈ શકે છે. Continuous mixer ની dispersion સામાન્ય રીતે separate gravity settler માં જાય છે. Mixer outlet બે-phase mixture છે; પોતે separated products નથી.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Feed તથા solvent controlled mixing હેઠળ મળે છે. એક phase ના droplets બીજી phase માં બની enlarged interface પરથી transfer થાય છે. Required residence time રાખો; vigorous mixing એટલે equilibrium ની ખાતરી નહીં. Dispersion settle કર્યા પછી phases અલગ withdraw થાય છે. Batch માં mixing/settling alternate થાય છે; continuous mixer–settler માં adjacent units આ functions જુદાં કરે છે. Excessive shear stable emulsions/carryover વધારી શકે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Stagewise extraction તથા mixer–settler cascade નો mixer section.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Power, sealing, emulsification તથા residence time મહત્વનાં છે. Actual use માટે hazardous-solvent SOP તથા rated containment જરૂરી છે.

body.en:
Definition

A low-velocity vessel separating a contacted liquid dispersion into light and heavy liquid layers by gravity.

Principle

Density difference causes droplets to rise or settle and coalesce when sufficient disengagement time is available.

Construction

A horizontal settling chamber receives dispersion through a calming inlet or baffle. It provides a quiet volume, an interface region and separate light/heavy outlets with level or interface control. Coalescing internals may be provided for a compatible duty, but they do not replace adequate residence time. The diagram labels light and heavy outlets; extract/raffinate identity is assigned according to which layer is solvent-rich.

Working

The mixed dispersion slows on entering the vessel. Droplets migrate under gravity and join their continuous layer, allowing a visible interface to develop. Light liquid leaves above the interface and heavy liquid from below it while outlet arrangements maintain the phase inventory. Settling is a separation step after extraction contact, not a fresh assumption of equilibrium transfer. Fine stable emulsions may remain dispersed and require different contacting/separation conditions rather than simply a higher outlet rate.

Applications

Phase disengagement in mixer–settler extraction and solvent-recovery sections.

Limitations and precautions

Small density difference, high viscosity and emulsions require more area/time. Interface control prevents product cross-contamination.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Gravity વડે contacted dispersion ને light/heavy liquid layers માં અલગ કરતું low-velocity vessel છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Density difference થી droplets rise/settle તથા coalesce થાય છે; પૂરતો disengagement time જોઈએ.

રચના (Construction)

Horizontal chamber માં calming inlet/baffle, quiet volume, interface region તથા separate light/heavy outlets અને level/interface control હોય છે. Compatible duty માટે coalescing internals હોઈ શકે છે; તે residence time નો વિકલ્પ નથી. Drawing light/heavy outlets બતાવે છે. Extract/raffinate identity solvent-rich layer મુજબ નક્કી થાય છે.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Mixed dispersion vessel માં ધીમી પડે છે. Droplets gravity હેઠળ move/coalesce થઈ interface બનાવે છે. Light liquid ઉપરથી અને heavy liquid નીચેથી નીકળે છે; outlets phase inventories જાળવે છે. Settling extraction contact પછીની separation step છે; તે equilibrium transfer ની આપોઆપ ખાતરી નથી. Fine stable emulsion માટે જુદી contacting/separation conditions જરૂરી થઈ શકે છે; વધુ outlet rate solution નથી.

ઉપયોગો

Mixer–settler extraction તથા solvent-recovery માં phase disengagement.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Small density difference, high viscosity તથા emulsion માટે વધુ area/time જોઈએ. Interface control cross-contamination ઘટાડે છે.

body.en:
Definition

A liquid–liquid contact column using perforated trays to distribute one liquid as droplets through the other.

Principle

Repeated droplet formation/contact and phase redistribution increase interfacial transfer between countercurrent liquids.

Construction

The shell carries perforated trays and passages/downcomers for the opposite continuous phase. In the illustrated arrangement, light dispersed solvent enters low and rises through tray holes; heavy feed enters high and passes downward through designated passages. End disengagement sections collect the separated phases with interface controls. Tray spacing and open area govern loading; these are liquid droplets, not gas bubbles as in an absorber.

Working

The light phase issues through perforations and disperses into the heavier continuous liquid. Solute partitions between phases during droplet travel and contact on successive tray levels. Heavy liquid flows downward while the light dispersed phase rises to a top separation zone. The bottom zone withdraws heavy product. Contacting is staged physically but each tray need not be ideal. When the density/continuous-phase choice is reversed, the feed ports and hydraulic arrangement must be redesigned accordingly.

Applications

Countercurrent liquid extraction where tray hydraulics and density difference are suitable.

Limitations and precautions

Flooding, phase inversion, entrainment and emulsion formation limit useful throughput.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Perforated trays વડે એક liquid ને બીજી liquid માં droplets તરીકે distribute કરતો extraction column છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Repeated droplet formation/contact તથા redistribution થી countercurrent liquids વચ્ચે interfacial transfer વધે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Shell માં perforated trays તથા opposite continuous phase માટે passages/downcomers છે. Drawing માં light dispersed solvent નીચેથી આવી holes માંથી ઊઠે છે. Heavy feed ઉપરથી designated passages માં નીચે જાય છે. End disengagement sections તથા interface controls separated phases એકત્ર કરે છે. Tray spacing/open area loading નક્કી કરે છે. અહીં liquid droplets છે, absorber જેવા gas bubbles નહીં.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Light phase holes માંથી dispersed droplets બનાવે છે. Droplet travel તથા successive tray contacts દરમિયાન solute phases વચ્ચે distribute થાય છે. Heavy liquid નીચે અને light droplets ઉપર જાય છે. Top/bottom separation zones થી products withdraw થાય છે. Physical stages છે, દરેક ideal હોવો જરૂરી નથી. Density/continuous-phase choice બદલાય તો ports/hydraulics પણ accordingly બદલવા પડે છે.

ઉપયોગો

Suitable tray hydraulics/density difference ધરાવતી countercurrent extraction.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Flooding, phase inversion, entrainment તથા emulsion useful throughput limit કરે છે.

body.en:
Definition

A differential liquid–liquid extractor using packing to distribute contacting phases over the column height.

Principle

Countercurrent liquid flow and repeated wetting/droplet renewal provide interfacial transfer without discrete equilibrium trays.

Construction

A vertical shell contains compatible packing, supports, phase distributors and enlarged end disengagement zones. For the illustrated light-solvent case, heavy feed enters above the bed and light solvent below it. Light and heavy outlets have interface control. Packing wetting and continuous/dispersed-phase choice must suit the actual liquids; the arrangement is not a gas absorber merely with its stream names changed.

Working

Light solvent moves upward through the packing while the heavy liquid flows downward. The distributed phases exchange solute along the bed and then disengage at the ends. In the stated example, the solvent-rich extract leaves from the light end and carrier-rich raffinate from the heavy end, but this product positioning reverses if solvent density reverses. Maldistribution reduces useful area, and excessive loading causes entrainment, flooding or phase inversion rather than guaranteed better transfer.

Applications

Continuous extraction with sufficiently clean liquids and favorable distribution/wetting.

Limitations and precautions

Fouling, emulsions, poor wetting and small density difference can make the duty unsuitable.

body.en:
Definition

A mechanically agitated vertical extraction column with rotating disks and stationary rings.

Principle

Controlled mechanical dispersion renews liquid interfaces while countercurrent flow provides the concentration progression.

Construction

The column contains a central driven shaft carrying spaced circular disks and a shell fitted with stationary ring baffles. The contacting section has feed/solvent inlets, while top and bottom disengagement zones provide separated outlets and interface control. A motor and suitable shaft seal drive the rotor. The stator rings divide circulation regions and limit excessive axial mixing; the disks are not perforated equilibrium trays.

Working

The rotor shears and circulates the liquid phases to form useful droplets and renew their surrounding films. Heavy and light streams move countercurrently through successive agitated regions while solute partitions between them. The end zones slow the dispersion so phases separate before withdrawal. Rotor speed affects droplet size, holdup, power and axial mixing; increasing speed indefinitely can cause emulsification or flooding rather than improved separation. The column still requires actual equilibrium data and residence-time/efficiency information.

Applications

Continuous liquid extraction requiring controlled mechanical dispersion.

Limitations and precautions

Moving parts, seals, power, axial mixing and emulsion sensitivity require suitable design/maintenance.

Motor તથા suitable shaft seal rotor ચલાવે છે. Stator rings circulation regions બનાવે છે તથા excessive axial mixing limit કરે છે. Disks perforated equilibrium trays નથી.

End zones dispersion ધીમી કરી withdrawal પહેલાં separation આપે છે. Speed થી droplet size, holdup, power તથા axial mixing બદલાય છે. Speed સતત વધારવાથી emulsion/flooding થઈ શકે છે. Actual equilibrium તથા residence-time/efficiency data જોઈએ.

ઉપયોગો

Controlled mechanical dispersion જરૂરી હોય તેવી continuous extraction.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Moving parts, seals, power, axial mixing તથા emulsion sensitivity માટે suitable design/maintenance જોઈએ.

body.en:
Definition

A compact contactor that combines liquid–liquid contacting with phase separation under centrifugal acceleration.

Principle

Mixing promotes solute transfer; rotation accelerates density-based phase separation without changing the equilibrium selectivity by itself.

Construction

A representative unit has a stationary housing, two liquid feeds, a mixing region, a rotating separating bowl and separate outlets controlled by internal weirs or passages. A motor, shaft, bearings and appropriate seals support the rotor. The schematic distinguishes the heavy outer layer from the lighter inner layer; exact inlet/rotor arrangements vary by design. These devices need balanced rotating assemblies and rated containment.

Working

Feed and solvent first form a contacted dispersion, allowing solute to approach its distribution relation. The mixture enters the rotating separation zone, where the denser liquid moves outward and the lighter liquid inward. Each layer follows its designated outlet path, producing separate phases rapidly compared with gravity settling alone. A single centrifugal unit is not automatically many ideal stages; multiple units may be cascaded for greater recovery or purity. Excessive solids, unstable hydraulics or poor mixing can still limit performance.

Applications

Compact extraction, short residence-time duties and difficult gravity disengagement when the fluids suit the rotor design.

Limitations and precautions

Rotor balance, speed rating, seals, power and solids tolerance matter; never infer safe operating limits from an educational sketch.

સિદ્ધાંત

Mixing transfer વધારેછે; rotation density-based separation ઝડપી બનાવે છે, પણ પોતે equilibrium selectivity બદલતું નથી.

રચના (Construction)

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Feed/solvent ની contacted dispersion માં solute distribution relation તરફ જાય છે. Rotating zone માં denser liquid બહાર તથા lighter liquid અંદર જાય છે. Designated outlet paths અલગ products આપે છે. Gravity settling કરતાં separation ઝડપી થઈ શકે છે. એક centrifugal unit આપોઆપ ઘણા ideal stages નથી; greater recovery/purity માટે units cascade થાય છે. Solids, unstable hydraulics અથવા poor mixing performance limit કરે છે.

Rotor-compatible fluids માટે compact extraction, short residence-time તથા difficult gravity disengagement duties.

Rotor balance, speed rating, seals, power તથા solids tolerance મહત્વનાં છે. Study sketch પરથી safe limits ન નક્કી કરો.

Objective and official scope

Measure actual extraction and compare it with an explicitly defined ideal-stage reference at the same inputs, temperature and basis. Keep recovery distinct from stage efficiency.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved immiscible feed/solvent pair, sealed contacting/settling apparatus, balance, temperature measurement and calibrated solute assay. Equilibrium endpoints/reference must be supplied or independently established.

Principle and assumptions

Use measured phase masses and solute fractions for product solute balances. The mixer must be followed by phase separation.

Procedure and record

Record feed and solvent masses, compositions, temperature, contact/settling conditions and both separated product masses/assays. Identify solvent-rich extract and carrier-rich raffinate rather than assigning names solely from layer position. Determine actual recovered solute and compare with the provided ideal reference. Account for holdup and samples.

Safety, quality and limitations

Use closed approved solvent handling and ventilation. Do not report recovery as efficiency without the ideal reference. No invented equilibrium compositions or observations.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Liquid–liquid extraction and industrial uses.
q.gu: Liquid–liquid Extraction તથા Industrial Uses ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Liquid–liquid extraction separates a dissolved solute by distributing it between the original liquid and another liquid solvent that creates two separable phases. Extract is the solvent-rich product; raffinate is the feed-carrier-rich product. The operation is useful when volatility differences are poor, heat-sensitive materials discourage distillation or a solvent provides useful selectivity. Applications include recovery of organic acids from aqueous streams, purification of selected chemical products and hydrometallurgical extraction using suitable extractants. The solvent normally requires downstream recovery; extraction alone does not necessarily give a pure solute. A light phase is not automatically the extract: which product is extract depends on solvent identity, while top/bottom location depends on density.
a.gu: Original liquid તથા બીજો solvent બે separable phases બનાવે અને solute તેમના વચ્ચે distribute થાય તે liquid–liquid extraction છે. Solvent-rich product extract અને feed-carrier-rich product raffinate છે. Volatility difference ઓછો હોય, heat-sensitive material હોય અથવા solvent useful selectivity આપે ત્યારે extraction ઉપયોગી છે. Aqueous streams માંથી organic acids recovery, chemical purification તથા suitable extractants વડે hydrometallurgical extraction examples છે. Downstream solvent recovery સામાન્ય રીતે જોઈએ; extraction માત્રથી pure solute મળતો નથી. Light phase હંમેશાં extract નથી. Extract solvent identity પરથી અને top/bottom density પરથી નક્કી થાય છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Liquid equilibrium,distribution and selectivity.
q.gu: Liquid Equilibrium,Distribution તથા Selectivity ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Liquid equilibrium specifies compositions of two coexisting liquid phases at given temperature and pressure. A tie line joins the conjugate equilibrium phase compositions. A distribution coefficient compares solute concentration in extract with that in raffinate on a declared basis. It can vary with composition, temperature and association; it is not universally constant. Selectivity compares separation of solute C from feed carrier A between phases. A solvent with high capacity may also dissolve much carrier and give poor selectivity. There must actually be two phases; one homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture cannot by itself define an interphase distribution coefficient. Water/organic systems need explicitly identified aqueous and organic phases.
a.gu: Given T, P પર બે coexisting liquid phases ની compositions liquid equilibrium દર્શાવે છે. Conjugate equilibrium compositions જોડતી line tie line છે. Declared basis પર extract તથા raffinate માં solute concentrations નો ratio distribution coefficient છે. Composition, T તથા association થી તે બદલાઈ શકે છે; universal constant નથી. Selectivity phases વચ્ચે solute C ને carrier A સામે અલગ કરવાની ક્ષમતા દર્શાવે છે. High-capacity solvent carrier પણ ઘણો dissolve કરે તો selectivity નબળી હોઈ શકે છે. બે phases હોવી જરૂરી છે. એક homogeneous binary solvent/acid mixture થી interphase coefficient નક્કી ન થાય. Aqueous તથા organic phases સ્પષ્ટ ઓળખો.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Equilateral triangular coordinates and lever rule.
q.gu: Equilateral Triangular Coordinates તથા Lever Rule ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: An equilateral ternary composition diagram represents mixtures of three components whose fractions add to one. A vertex represents a pure component and the opposite side represents zero fraction of that component. Read a component fraction along lines parallel to the side opposite its vertex. Always identify component names, temperature and mass or mole basis; do not mix the bases. A binary mixture lies on an edge and a ternary mixture lies inside. A mixing point M for streams F and S lies on their straight joining line, closer to the larger stream. The splitting of M into conjugate E and R lies along a measured tie line, not along an arbitrary line to a vertex. Lever-rule product ratios use opposite segment lengths. Mixing line and equilibrium tie line are different geometric objects.
a.gu: ત્રણ components ના fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોય તેવી compositions equilateral ternary diagram દર્શાવે છે. Vertex pure component તથા opposite side તે component નો zero fraction છે. Vertex ની opposite side ને parallel lines વડે fraction વાંચો. Component names, T તથા mass/mole basis લખો; બંને bases mix ન કરો. Binary mixture edge પર અને ternary mixture અંદર આવે છે. F તથા S નું mixing point M straight joining line પર તથા larger stream ની નજીક આવે છે. M ના E, R products measured tie line પર હોય છે; vertex તરફ arbitrary line નહીં. Lever rule માં opposite segment lengths નો ratio લેવાય છે. Mixing line તથા equilibrium tie line જુદાં છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Three liquids:one partially soluble pair and T/P effects.
q.gu: Three Liquids:One Partially Soluble Pair તથા T/P અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A Type-I ternary system has one binary pair with limited mutual solubility, while the third component is mutually miscible with the other two over the stated range. The partially miscible pair creates a miscibility gap whose ternary boundary is the binodal curve. Compositions within the two-phase region split along tie lines; the two branches approach one another at a plait point where the phase distinction disappears. Tie lines are generally not horizontal and their slopes must come from data. For many upper-critical-solution-temperature systems, heating shrinks the miscibility gap, but lower-critical and more complex behavior also exist; do not claim that temperature always increases mutual solubility. Ordinary pressure has a smaller effect on nearly incompressible liquid equilibrium, unless high pressure, gas solubility or special phase behavior is involved. The diagram here is schematic, not measured acetic-acid/benzene/water data.
a.gu: Stated range માં એક binary pair limited mutual solubility ધરાવે અને third component બંને સાથે miscible હોય તે Type-I ternary system છે. Partially miscible pair થી miscibility gap બને છે; તેની ternary boundary binodal curve છે. Two-phase region નું mixture tie line અનુસાર split થાય છે. Plait point પાસે બંને phases નો difference અદૃશ્ય થાય છે. Tie lines હંમેશાં horizontal નથી; actual data જોઈએ. ઘણા upper-critical systems માં heating થી gap ઘટે છે, પરંતુ lower-critical/complex behavior પણ હોય છે. Temperature થી miscibility હંમેશાં વધે એવું ન કહો. Nearly incompressible liquids પર ordinary pressure ની અસર સામાન્ય રીતે ઓછી છે; high pressure/gas solubility/special behavior exceptions છે. આ schematic છે, measured acid/benzene/water data નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Three liquids:two partially soluble pairs.
q.gu: Three Liquids:Two Partially Soluble Pairs ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A Type-II ternary system has two binary pairs with limited mutual solubility at the specified conditions. Miscibility gaps therefore appear on two binary edges rather than only one. The two-phase region and its conjugate branches must be obtained from equilibrium data; they need not resemble the simple Type-I cap or share its plait-point construction. Tie lines still join coexisting phases and all phase compositions must sum to one. The number of partially miscible binary pairs does not by itself imply three liquid phases. The supplied diagram is a topology sketch identifying the two affected edges, not a source of quantitative stage compositions.
a.gu: Specified conditions પર બે binary pairs limited mutual solubility ધરાવે તે Type-II ternary system છે. બે binary edges પર miscibility gaps મળે છે. Two-phase region તથા conjugate branches actual equilibrium data પરથી નક્કી કરો; તે Type-I cap/plait construction જેવી હોવી જરૂરી નથી. Tie lines coexisting phases જોડે છે અને phase fractions નો સરવાળો 1 હોવો જોઈએ. બે partially miscible binary pairs એટલે ત્રણ liquid phases નહીં. Sketch બે affected edges ઓળખાવે છે; quantitative stage compositions માટે data નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Choice of extraction solvent.
q.gu: Extraction Solvent ની પસંદગી ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: An extraction solvent must create a favorable solute distribution and sufficiently separable liquid phases while remaining recoverable and safe. Evaluate selectivity, capacity, mutual solubility with feed carrier, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, chemical stability and ease of regeneration. Adequate density difference helps settling; very stable emulsions or low interfacial tension may hinder disengagement. Low viscosity aids transfer and pumping, but solvent loss/product contamination may still dominate economics. Include toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost and compatibility. A high distribution coefficient alone is insufficient if the solvent is difficult to separate or recover.
a.gu: Favorable solute distribution તથા separable phases સાથે recoverable અને safe હોય તે extraction solvent પસંદ કરવો. Selectivity, capacity, feed carrier સાથે mutual solubility, density difference, interfacial tension, viscosity, stability તથા regeneration જુઓ. Density difference settling ને મદદ કરે છે. Stable emulsion/low interfacial tension disengagement મુશ્કેલ કરી શકે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping સુધારે છે પણ solvent loss/contamination ખર્ચાળ હોઈ શકે છે. Toxicity, flammability, corrosion, availability, cost તથા compatibility ગણો. High distribution coefficient માત્ર પૂરતો નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Agitated extraction vessel.
q.gu: Agitated Extraction Vessel ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A mechanically mixed vessel that disperses one liquid phase in another to create extraction contact; phase separation completes the stage. Agitation increases interfacial area and renews the liquid films so solute moves toward its equilibrium distribution.
a.gu: એક liquid phase ને બીજામાં disperse કરીને extraction contact આપતું mechanically mixed vessel છે. Phase separation થી stage પૂર્ણ થાય છે. Agitation interfacial area વધારી liquid films renew કરે છે; solute equilibrium distribution તરફ જાય છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Gravity settler.
q.gu: Gravity Settler ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A low-velocity vessel separating a contacted liquid dispersion into light and heavy liquid layers by gravity. Density difference causes droplets to rise or settle and coalesce when sufficient disengagement time is available.
a.gu: Gravity વડે contacted dispersion ને light/heavy liquid layers માં અલગ કરતું low-velocity vessel છે. Density difference થી droplets rise/settle તથા coalesce થાય છે; પૂરતો disengagement time જોઈએ.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Sieve-tray extraction tower.
q.gu: Sieve-tray Extraction Tower ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A liquid–liquid contact column using perforated trays to distribute one liquid as droplets through the other. Repeated droplet formation/contact and phase redistribution increase interfacial transfer between countercurrent liquids.
a.gu: Perforated trays વડે એક liquid ને બીજી liquid માં droplets તરીકે distribute કરતો extraction column છે. Repeated droplet formation/contact તથા redistribution થી countercurrent liquids વચ્ચે interfacial transfer વધે છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Packed extraction tower.
q.gu: Packed Extraction Tower ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A differential liquid–liquid extractor using packing to distribute contacting phases over the column height. Countercurrent liquid flow and repeated wetting/droplet renewal provide interfacial transfer without discrete equilibrium trays.
a.gu: Column height દરમિયાન contacting liquids distribute કરવા packing વાપરતો differential extractor છે. Countercurrent liquid flow તથા wetting/droplet renewal discrete equilibrium trays વગર transfer આપે છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Rotating disk contactor (RDC).
q.gu: Rotating Disk Contactor (RDC) ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A mechanically agitated vertical extraction column with rotating disks and stationary rings. Controlled mechanical dispersion renews liquid interfaces while countercurrent flow provides the concentration progression.
a.gu: Rotating disks તથા stationary rings ધરાવતો mechanically agitated vertical extraction column છે. Controlled mechanical dispersion interfaces renew કરે છે અને countercurrent flow concentration progression આપે છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Centrifugal extractor.
q.gu: Centrifugal Extractor ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A compact contactor that combines liquid–liquid contacting with phase separation under centrifugal acceleration. Mixing promotes solute transfer; rotation accelerates density-based phase separation without changing the equilibrium selectivity by itself.
a.gu: Liquid–liquid contacting તથા centrifugal acceleration હેઠળ phase separation જોડતું compact contactor છે. Mixing transfer વધારેછે; rotation density-based separation ઝડપી બનાવે છે, પણ પોતે equilibrium selectivity બદલતું નથી.
